contexts.text: These Knowledges are described by sailors, etc.
Ships = doctrinals from the Word: hence it is evident what pilot, sailor, and sea, signify.
The ship-masters and sailors () = those who contribute, who are called laymen.

Every ship-master = the highest of them = emperors, kings, etc. Everyone employed upon ships = those in various functions in a higher or lower degree. Sailors () = the lowest, called the common people. (Explained.)
Than a Ship's rope can enter the eye of a needle.
They turn everything that is spoken of into what is filthy, as is the custom of many of the common people - sailors and the like. (Their correspondence.)
Those who teach, lead, and rule, are meant by the sailors, etc. ().
The sailors () = the ministers; the shipmasters, the leaders who lead and teach.
The sailors () = those in knowledge (as distinguished from those in intelligence, and those in wisdom. Compare AR 786, above.)

On charity in sailors. Sailors become charities if they look to the Lord, and shun evils as sins, while they do their work sincerely, justly, and faithfully... They do goods in no other way, continuously, than in their own work which is enjoined upon them, which is that of a seaman... Then they do not fear death; because if they die, they die in the Lord, and come into Heaven... I exhort sailors, also, ... to approach the Lord, and pray to Him; because there is no other God of sky, land, and sea.
